anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: AG-8 — Resilience to data-shape and data-scale change: widening the data basis (deeper history) must never crash an existing page or exhaust a service's memory; the UI degrades gracefully (contained error boundary, honest '—'/NA placeholder, never a blank/frozen frame); unbounded whole-table ORM loads forbidden on the deep basis.
anti_goal_violations.evidence: ORIGIN (iter-7): during a heavy ingest on the grown live dev DB the backend exhausted its enforced memory_cap_mb=6144 ulimit -v ceiling (worker-thread MemoryError), GET /api/health hung 7+ minutes (all 22 threads futex_do_wait), the UI froze on 'Checking backend...' instead of the honest 'Backend unavailable', and recovery required a MANUAL restart (evidence: iter-7 raw .llm.md UT-J-05 + J-05-backend-hung-checking.png + logs/backend.log MemoryError signature). Human-acknowledged; iter-8 was the sanctioned recovery. RESOLVED ITER-9 on the qualified evidence iter-8 could not produce. (1) The fix is real: four `except MemoryError` early-abort branches (data_manager.py:3049/3143/3186/3245) + the audit's post-bar-cache release (:3067-3068), 10 injected-MemoryError tests with a negative control. (2) The measurement iter-8 owed was RUN, owner-authorized, on a cooled host (Tctl 41C idle, 1Hz sampler live, thermal watchdog armed and never tripped): a full-universe rebuild immediately followed by a second heavy backfill in ONE long-lived process — the literal iter-7 scenario — for 1092.93s, both jobs status 'ok' with all seven aggregate categories, 439/439 GET /api/health polls HTTP 200 (median 0.398s, max 3.646s, zero timeouts, zero hangs, no manual restart), peak VmPeak 4,738,948 KB = 24.7% under the 6,291,456 KB cap, max Tctl 81C, no host reset. Evaluator independently re-derived every headline number from the retained raw files (runs/goal-ops-hardening-iter-9/heavy-ingest-vm-samples.csv 4,347 rows, -health.csv 439 rows all 200, -hwmon.csv, -pytest.log '1 passed in 1092.93s'); the reviewer and auditor did so separately. (3) iter-8's own attribution objection is CLOSED: the caps were applied by THIS iteration's shipped launcher block, evidenced by the measured process's own boot line (logs/backend.log:24243-24245 'host-guard: cpu_list=0-3,8-11 blas_threads=4'), not inherited from a pump session. (4) Independent corroboration from a different lane: browser-qa's live 4-minute 412-day chunked backfill kept /api/health at 200 with RSS ~4.2GB of the cap. WATCH ITEM carried forward (NOT a violation): the VmPeak margin narrowed 43.6% -> 24.7%, and the audit (P1) proved the benign sampling-cadence explanation impossible — VmPeak is a monotone kernel high-water mark and re-subsampling the trace at 1 Hz / 10s yields the identical peak — so peak demand genuinely grew and must be re-measured as the basis deepens.

anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: AG-10 — Host resource ceiling (hardware protection): heavy compute MUST be launched only via the project launch scripts (scripts/dev.sh / scripts/start-backend.sh), and those scripts MUST apply the host caps declared in project-extensions/host-guard/host-guard.env whenever that file is present (CPU-affinity mask, BLAS/OMP thread caps, memory_cap_mb, malloc_arena_max).
anti_goal_violations.evidence: OBSERVED (not introduced) at iter-8: host-guard.env was present but start-backend.sh applied only ulimit -v + MALLOC_ARENA_MAX (no taskset, no BLAS/OMP caps) and dev.sh applied no caps at all. RESOLVED ITER-9, the in-scope launcher work goal.md itself scheduled. Both scripts now carry a marked HOST-GUARD block that sources host-guard.env when present and HOST_GUARD_ENABLED=1, applies `taskset -c "$HOST_GUARD_CPU_LIST"` and exports OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=$HOST_GUARD_BLAS_THREADS; dev.sh's BACKEND SUBSHELL ONLY additionally mirrors the config-derived ulimit -v + MALLOC_ARENA_MAX (same app.config.get_config() values, computed once — no second derivation). Every value comes from host-guard.env; no magic numbers (evaluator read the hunks in iter-9/iter-diff.md:787-868). Absent file or HOST_GUARD_ENABLED=0 leaves behavior unchanged (TC-9). LIVE-VERIFIED by three independent readers on real processes: browser-qa on the running backend (/proc/1214476: Cpus_allowed_list 0-3,8-11, OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, Max address space 6442450944), the audit's own /proc trace, and TC-7/TC-8 — with TC-8 also proving the `next dev` FRONTEND subshell carries NONE of the caps (it needs the address space). Nothing was stripped or weakened. Carried non-blocking: audit B3 recommends a `command -v taskset` guard; flipping HOST_GUARD_REQUIRE_MARKERS 0 -> 1 remains owner/framework work, explicitly out of product scope.
